The post of Collector (District Collector) in India was created by Warren Hastings in 1772 [d1][d3][d6]. More specifically, the post was created on May 14, 1772, by the East India Company, of which Warren Hastings was the then Governor-General of India [d2][d6]. The Office of Collector, as set up by Warren Hastings, originally held judicial, executive, and revenue powers [d5]. In spite of many structural changes over the years, the district collector remained the most decisive officer of administration throughout the British period [d7].
